title: Dzvin.co — solutions for teams, individuals and research
lead: Dzvin.co helps HR and leaders move from fragmented questionnaires toward continuous review of team wellbeing patterns and a structured response to risk signals.

articles.title: From signals to team action
articles.summary: How Dzvin.co connects team-level patterns with a managed response

sections.title: A clearer picture of team wellbeing
paragraphs: Dzvin.co helps HR and leaders move from fragmented questionnaires toward continuous review of team wellbeing patterns and a structured response to risk signals.

Its core B2B offer combines organization structure and permissions, permitted group views, trends, risk events and manager workflows. Separate personal and research experiences support ongoing observations and structured study programs.

sections.title: When an organization already runs surveys
paragraphs: A survey often ends at a report. Dzvin.co focuses on ongoing context: how group-level signals change, which events require review and what happens next.
This does not guarantee a reduction in burnout. Assess pilot outcomes such as time to review, participation consistency and workflow quality.

sections.title: Personal and research experiences
paragraphs: Individual check-ins, practices and history form the personal journey. Research projects and cohorts support structured program evaluations.
Evaluate the experience that fits your role and current business challenge.

articles.title: Who Dzvin.co serves
articles.summary: Organizations first, with separate personal and research use cases

sections.title: Built for distinct audiences
paragraphs: The main commercial audience is an organization seeking a more systematic approach to team wellbeing. HR and People Operations typically work with line managers and budget owners when considering a pilot.

Individuals can use check-ins, history, practices and goals. Research organizations can manage projects, cohorts, access, historic records and export requests. These are different use cases with different success measures.

sections.title: HR and People Operations
paragraphs: Understand team-level trends, investigate potential sources of pressure and set appropriate support priorities.
Evaluate observation coverage, time to review a signal and workflow follow-through, not just a single average score.

sections.title: Team leaders
paragraphs: Work with permitted groups, review patterns and inspect specific risk events.
Administrators manage structure, membership and access rights. Available information is role-dependent.

sections.title: Research partners
paragraphs: Manage cohorts and participants, historical observations, inspection, exports and audit history.
Program evaluations need a defined protocol and actual evidence beyond dashboard availability.

articles.title: What Dzvin.co can do
articles.summary: Personal, organizational and research capabilities without inflated claims

sections.title: What the product offers
paragraphs: For organizations: teams and subgroups, invitations, role-scoped views, period and group filters, aggregated indicators, risk-event feeds and manager follow-up actions.

For individuals: stress, mood, energy and focus check-ins, records, questionnaires, history, practices and goals. For research: projects, participants, cohorts, historical datasets, inspection, export requests and audit trail.

sections.title: The team workflow
paragraphs: An authorized manager sees summary data, permitted team trends and a feed of risk events. Events support details, follow-up and resolution according to permissions.
This is decision support for responsible people, not independent automated personnel decisions.

sections.title: Boundaries and availability
paragraphs: The experience varies by role, data and project settings. A listed feature is not necessarily enabled for every account.
Validate any particular end-to-end scenario in an appropriate demo environment before rollout.

articles.title: How Dzvin.co works
articles.summary: Three product journeys to verify during a demonstration

sections.title: Three real product journeys
paragraphs: Organization: a manager opens their permitted view, selects a period and groups, reviews changing metrics, opens a risk event and records the next action. This demonstrates an operational workflow.
Individual: check-in → history → practice → another check-in. Research: project → membership and cohort → history → inspection → export request → audit. Screen access depends on account role.

sections.title: Organization walkthrough
paragraphs: Company overview → group filters → trend → risk event → context → manager follow-up.
The demonstration should use authorized data and avoid revealing identifiable employee histories.

sections.title: Individual walkthrough
paragraphs: Daily check-in → history → exercise or goal → repeat observation.
Value is continuity; an exercise's effect is not guaranteed.

sections.title: Research walkthrough
paragraphs: Research Workspace → project → membership and cohort → historic data → inspection → export request → audit.
Availability depends on research roles and program permissions.

articles.title: Business value and costs
articles.summary: A transparent pilot scenario calculator, not a fabricated ROI estimate

sections.title: Assess business value without invented savings
paragraphs: For an organizational pilot the question is not how many charts exist, but whether timely review and coordinated follow-up lead to a measurable operational outcome.

The scenario calculator below relies on user-entered assumptions only: participants, hourly cost, observed hours recovered, illustrative platform spend and setup cost. It is not an official price or a guaranteed return forecast.

sections.title: Metrics for a pilot
paragraphs: Compare before and after: time to review a signal, rate of events with a documented follow-up, repeated participation and process administration costs.
Use comparable baselines and actual company costs when translating outcomes into money.

sections.title: Cost components
paragraphs: Consider licenses, setup, managers' time and support. Commercial terms and scope should be agreed separately.
The calculator is for scenario assessment, not a quote.

articles.title: Comparing approaches
articles.summary: Dzvin.co alongside one-off surveys and standalone dashboards

sections.title: How the approach differs
paragraphs: A one-off survey produces a snapshot. A standalone corporate dashboard may surface trends without an event-handling workflow. Dzvin.co connects repeated observations, group-level views and a manager workflow in its documented product surface.
This is a category comparison, not a measured ranking of named competitors. Evaluate any alternative against your organization's exact requirements and a live workflow.

sections.title: Evaluation criteria
paragraphs: Compare observation frequency, group-level insight, access rules, event workflows, research capability and export availability.
A meaningful comparison needs the same real workflow across solutions.

sections.title: Questions for a demo
paragraphs: Can a manager see only permitted groups? Can an event be followed through to action? What happens when data is missing? Which pilot metrics are available?
These are evaluation questions, not claims about named competitors.

articles.title: Dzvin.co presentations
articles.summary: Three finished audience-specific decks, printable to PDF

sections.title: Explore Dzvin.co through presentations
paragraphs: The organization deck follows signal → team context → priority → action → review. The individual deck follows the daily observation journey. The research deck explains a controlled program workflow.
Open one of the three decks below. Present directly in a browser or save to PDF using the print control. No fabricated customers, success percentages or confidential engineering claims are included.

sections.title: Organization deck
paragraphs: Business problem → team signal → managed response → measurement → pilot. Each deck is a browser-based slide presentation.
Use the print control to save the slides as a PDF if needed.

sections.title: Individual and research decks
paragraphs: Personal: regular observations and accessible next steps. Research: cohorts, records, reporting and traceability.
Each presentation leads with the primary customer journey for that audience.

articles.title: Pilot and rollout
articles.summary: Define the evaluation design and success criteria

sections.title: Pilot design and success criteria
paragraphs: Begin with one measurable challenge: for example, reducing the time between a team-level signal and a responsible person's review. Agree on the cohort, access, observation window and evaluation criteria before rollout.

Useful pilot indicators include repeated participation, data completeness, time to review and event handling. For individuals, track repeated check-ins; for research, collection wave completion and traceability. These are suggested metrics, not proven Dzvin.co outcomes.

sections.title: Pilot design
paragraphs: Choose an owner, sample, observation window, permissions and measurement approach. Record a baseline before starting.
A pilot should test a concrete workflow hypothesis, not just show screens.

sections.title: Decision after a pilot
paragraphs: Compare outcomes with agreed criteria, assess the cost of rollout and decide the appropriate scope.
If evidence is incomplete, reflect that in the conclusion.

articles.title: Getting started
articles.summary: What the service does and how to begin

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Dzvin.co helps people record stress, mood, energy and focus, review trends and find potentially useful wellbeing activities.
There are separate experiences for individuals, organizations and research programs.

sections.title: First steps
paragraphs: Create an account or sign in. Open My Day, complete a short self-check and review the available guidance.
Check in consistently. Trends matter more than a single daily score.

sections.title: Interpreting results
paragraphs: A single response reflects one moment, not your overall health.
Some functionality is limited by role or release stage.

sections.title: Daily checks
paragraphs: The standard check-in covers stress, mood, energy and focus on a 1–5 scale.
Notes and repeated observations offer context, but cannot establish causation.

sections.title: Suggestions and exercises
paragraphs: Relevant exercises and suggestions may follow a check-in. Personal features also support viewing history and goals.
Compare periods rather than trying to optimize one number.

sections.title: Questionnaires
paragraphs: Short psychological questionnaires may help with self-reflection.
They do not establish a diagnosis or prescribe treatment.

sections.title: Organizational use
paragraphs: The team experience helps analyze group-level changes in stress, energy and wellbeing.
Available reports and access depend on user permissions and organization settings.

sections.title: Acting on signals
paragraphs: A risk signal should prompt further contextual review, not an automated judgement about an employee.
Do not make personnel decisions from one aggregate metric. Small groups may still permit re-identification.

sections.title: Responsibilities
paragraphs: Organizations remain responsible for appropriate legal grounds for processing and transparent staff communication.
Aggregation alone does not ensure anonymity.

articles.title: Research and validation
articles.summary: Cohorts, repeated observations and evidence quality

sections.title: Research workflows
paragraphs: Research scenarios include cohort comparisons, repeated measurements and program outcome reviews.
Access to a feature does not imply independent clinical validation of every model.

sections.title: Evidence quality
paragraphs: Specify samples, metrics, windows, missing-data handling and quality criteria before analysis.
Separate correlation, prediction and causal effects. Report uncertainty.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Research partnerships, data scope and publishing terms are agreed separately.
Ethics and privacy requirements remain applicable.

articles.title: Privacy and data
articles.summary: Data processing, access and user rights

sections.title: Your data
paragraphs: The service may process account information, voluntary assessments and product interactions.
The current Privacy Policy defines the precise categories, purposes and legal basis.

sections.title: Workplace access
paragraphs: Organizational reports must respect permissions and applicable privacy rules.
Avoid entering unnecessary sensitive details and never share account credentials.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Use official Dzvin.co contacts to request access, correction or deletion of personal data.
This guide does not replace the Privacy Policy or Terms of Service.

articles.title: Capabilities and limitations
articles.summary: What indicators and predictions can and cannot establish

sections.title: Uncertainty
paragraphs: Self-reports may be incomplete, biased or context-dependent. Forecasts and risk indicators do not guarantee outcomes.
Recommendations are not proof of causal effects.

sections.title: Medical boundary
paragraphs: Dzvin.co is not an emergency service. It does not diagnose conditions or replace medical or psychological care.
For an immediate safety or health emergency, contact local emergency services.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: Some reports and modules may be role-restricted or not generally available while the product evolves.
For current availability, consult the FAQ or support team.

featuredNote: For organizations: team-level signals, decision-support workflows and measurable evaluation. Separate personal and research experiences are also available.
